what: First Industrial Realty Trust is a REIT that owns and develops industrial buildings: warehouses, distribution centres and smaller light-industrial properties, concentrated in a set of major US logistics markets.
customers: Logistics companies, retailers and manufacturers who need space to store and move goods, from regional distributors taking a small building to large tenants leasing a whole facility.
money: Leases on warehouse and light-industrial buildings, with annual rent increases and tenants paying most operating costs.
moat: Industrial land in established logistics corridors near large cities is limited, and permitting new warehouses is slow. Leases signed years ago are often well below current market rents, so each renewal raises income without any new investment.
risks: A large amount of new warehouse space was delivered across the US, so vacancy has risen and the pace of rent increases has slowed.
Debt of about $2.6B against $78.0M of cash means refinancing at higher rates reduces distributable cash.
The shares trade at about 9.2 times sales and 18.2 times EV/EBITDA, full prices for a REIT in a softening leasing market.
Development projects are started before tenants are signed, so a weak market leaves empty new buildings.
Tenant concentration in logistics means an e-commerce slowdown affects many tenants at once.
opportunities: Rents on expiring leases are still well below current market levels in many markets, so renewals lift income mechanically.
Revenue has grown every year shown, from $476.3M in 2021 to $727.1M in 2025.
New construction starts have fallen sharply across the industry, which historically tightens the market a year or two later.
Sixteen analysts average a $64.38 target, about 20% above the current price.
watch: The spread between expiring rents and new lease rents. That single figure determines how much income growth is already locked into the existing portfolio, regardless of what the wider market does.
